meta.gift: warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls
meta.waning: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down
meta.curse_desc: a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out
veils: The rites of rekindling consume souls faster than the Ember returns them, and the church keeps the arithmetic hidden.
The Ember is not dying — the gods siphon it to prolong their reign, and the curse is the siphon's residue.
The siphon was the Ember's own bargain: it feeds the gods so that something older, asleep in its heart, stays asleep. The gods know, and keep feeding.
meta.epigraph: Of the First Ember little now is spoken, and less is true. Gather what the old things still remember, and be sparing with belief.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the First Ember gave the world warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the First Ember rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world warmth, disparity, and the colour of souls.

e2.text: Yorthas, god of the hunt and the mercy of endings, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Ruthmere, god of storms and unkept promises, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Mazannoth, god of healing and the price of healing, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e6.text: The Brand of Yorthas was wrought as regalia of Yorthas's throne.

e8.text: The Pyre of Ruthmere was wrought as regalia of Ruthmere's throne.

e10.text: The Cinder of Mazannoth was wrought as regalia of Mazannoth's throne.

e11.text: Eloros, the Cinder-Eater, rose against the thrones. Yorthas led the gods to war.
e11.hidden: Ruthmere treated with Eloros in secret and was spared what followed.

e12.text: Eloros was defeated and sealed beneath Hestanaramarch; the seal was bought with the lives of 7 champions.

e13.text: The waning began: the Ember gutters; shadows lengthen and the dead forget to lie down. Mortals called the affliction the Gutter-mark: a grey brand that spreads over the heart; the marked wander until their names burn out.

e14.text: Ruthgrim the Forsworn founded the Order of the Ember at Elaegargate, sworn to stand against the Gutter-mark.

e15.text: The Church of Ruthmere was raised at Hareastvault; Eloach the Twice-crowned took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e16.text: Queluveth of the Last Door was cast out of Church of Ruthmere and founded the Cult of the Open Door, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e16.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e17.text: Mazirdis the Adamant united the river-clans and was crowned in Fenearamere; the realm took the name Morulaspire.

e18.text: At the urging of Eloach, the saint Kariadane Half-remembered was given to the First Ember in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e18.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Eloach suspected as much.

e19.text: Oloula the Lantern-eyed, sword-hand of Mazirdis, opened the gates of Fenearamere to the Order of the Ember over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e19.hidden: Oloula acted on a promise from the Cult of the Open Door: that the marked of their house would be spared the Gutter-mark. The promise was not kept.

e20.text: Morulaspire fell. Mazirdis the Adamant died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e21.text: Oloula was found at Wrenrionspire bearing the Gutter-mark, and was not spared.

e22.text: Ruthmere, god of storms and unkept promises, took the Gutter-mark — the first of the gods to bear it — and wandered from their seat.
e22.hidden: The curse does not distinguish gods from mortals. It never did.

e23.text: Banudane the Latecomer, last-sworn of the Order of the Ember, set out for the place where Ruthmere was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e24.text: Word came that Banudane fell to the marked, and then word came that Banudane led the marked. The order believes neither.

e25.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the Open Door were found digging at the seal of Eloros. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e25.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.
